How the ranking works

The default order uses the strongest dated public company-value signal available: current market capitalization, announced transaction value, then a last disclosed or clearly derived private valuation. These measures are visibly labeled because they are not economically identical.

Bounded ranges are sorted by their midpoint; “greater than” values sort just above the stated floor; exact ties share a rank and are alphabetized. The visible label—not the internal sort key—is the reported economic claim.

A record enters the ranked index only after the founder’s UT relationship, founder role, and value or funding figure are each supported by public evidence. Austin location alone does not count. Funding is never presented as valuation.

Values change. Public-company figures use the latest trading-day data available during the September 2026 review; private valuations and acquisitions retain their original announcement dates.

“Every founder” is not a mathematically provable claim: private companies can hide both funding and founder biographies, and no authoritative university-wide founder registry exists. This site is therefore a reproducible, public-source census. It favors false-negative omissions over weakly sourced inclusion.
